items.heading: "Tier 2 College" Is Not
items.text: "Tier 2 college" is not an official government category, it is informal shorthand students and recruiters use, usually meaning any college outside the flagship IIT/NIT/IIM/AIIMS bracket, often located in a tier 2 or tier 3 city by population.

items.heading: Numbers Work Better Than Vague
items.text: Numbers work better than vague reassurance here. This is what current reporting shows across the tier 1 versus tier 2 divide.

items.heading: Register on Fresher
items.text: Register on fresher-specific platforms early , not only in final year, many list opportunities filtered by graduation year, branch, and skill set well before campus season starts.

items.heading: Take Open National Qualifier
items.text: Take open national qualifier-style tests run by large employers, since these accept applicants from any college and test on merit directly.

items.heading: Build One Portfolio Piece That
items.text: Build one portfolio piece that solves a real, specific problem , a project tied to an actual Indian use case reads stronger to a recruiter than a generic tutorial clone.

items.heading: Use Warm Outreach, Not Cold
items.text: Use warm outreach, not cold spam , a short, specific message to an alum or a professional in your target field, with one relevant proof link and one small question, consistently outperforms mass-applying to unrelated roles.

items.heading: IT Either Denies the Placement
items.text: It either denies the placement gap exists, which insults your intelligence, or treats tier 2 as a permanent ceiling, which is simply false.

items.heading: IT Rarely Explains Which Specific
items.text: It rarely explains which specific routes are brand-blind by design, so students waste a year assuming every door needs a tier 1 name.

items.heading: IT Skips Real Placement
items.text: It skips real placement and package numbers, leaving students to guess instead of plan against actual data.

items.heading: IT Treats "Get More Certificates"
items.text: It treats "get more certificates" as the answer instead of naming the real lever: one deep skill plus visible, verifiable proof of work.
